note: Twelve measured regions, twelve accounted: four figure items and eight exclusions. The paper prints exactly four numbered figures and all four are measured. The eight exclusions are typeset Java listings, one of them a whole appendix page (Boat.java) and one the tail of the next (River.java), which the layout pass measures as vector regions because their code text draws paths; paper 8 settled that a program listing is no exhibit. Declared gap: eight further pages carry code paths the layout pass leaves unmeasured (p6, p18, p20, p21, p22, p23, p24, p25), and those listing bodies are not counted anywhere; the appendix of source code runs from p17 to the end of the document.
rules: Eight of the twelve measured regions are typeset Java listings - p5, p7, p9, p10, p17, p19 twice and p26 - so they are excluded not-an-exhibit and the paper has four figure items [place.area_frac].
Figures 1 and 2 are two side-by-side raster images on one baseline, each with its own printed number and its own caption paragraph under it [caption.verbatim].

Figures 1 and 2 are drawn state grids with raft glyphs and printed cell text, no axes and no tick numbers, so they are flowchart-or-schematic with printed_numbers false and data_labels true [geometry.printed_numbers] [geometry.data_labels].
Figure 3 is a marker-only plot with grey gridlines and no legend, so it is scatter [geometry.family].
Figure 4 has a smooth fitted quadratic drawn through its markers and prints the fit and its R^2 inside the frame, so it is line and data_labels is true [geometry.family] [geometry.data_labels].
Only Figure 4 is cited in running text ('As can be seen in Figure 4'), on the page that prints it; Figures 1-3 are read only through their captions [mention.lead_sentence].

The heading index is made of code lines ('87 Boat temp = nextBoat;' and the like), so every section_path here is an unnumbered heading copied from the text layer and section_numbered is false [place.section_path].
Figure 4's printed caption runs on into the paper's prose, so the quote stops at the sentence break before 'Rowing more than 12 hours is not realistic' [caption.words].
